doc.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Road memories, photos, neighborhood and church
title: Closing thanks to Taylor
summary: Taylor and Hinton thank each other, with Hinton saying he feels lonely talking about the old days.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Uncle Henry‟s, right. Well Milt, thank you very much. This has been really very enjoyable for me and the idea of having someone of your stature just reminisce and talk about history in the first person I think is very important.
Well thank you. It‟s nice to be able to talk to somebody about it that has

some research about it and has some semblance of it. I feel kind of lonely out here sometimes. I don‟t want to talk about things that people don‟t… I find that about young bass players, there‟s not much [unintelligible] or Rufus Reed, some of the intricate things that we do, we don‟t want to talk about bass wise. I‟m afraid to get into because I don‟t want to bore anybody. But then when we get into things and say well here‟s a thing that I just found, it‟s wonderful and this is the kind of thing that I‟m enjoying with you and I thank you a million for this. I hope it will be of some use to somebody.
I‟m sure it will be. I know it‟s been of use to me because you told me a lot of things I certainly didn‟t know. Thank you.
